_doc: HMTc Category 5 (Beverages) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit-only: every published number in this file is the strictest applicable maximum level set by a credible sovereign government for that exact (product form, analyte) cell in the row's native basis, a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign cell where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination, or a control. Nothing here is occurrence-derived: no percentile, no floor, no precautionary or feasibility adjustment. Every number is named by a regulatory_limit_id in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv and is resolved by the compiler, never written into this config by hand. The instrument families that govern this category are: EU 2023/915 (fruit-juice lead sections 3.1.19.1 and 3.1.19.2, fruit-juice inorganic arsenic section 3.4.4, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks inorganic arsenic section 3.4.1.6, cocoa-powder cadmium section 3.2.15.4, canned-beverage inorganic tin section 3.5.2); EU 2024/1987 (nickel in juices and nectars, and in cocoa powder, applying from 1 July 2025); Codex CXS 193 (fruit and grape juices, canned foods); US FDA (final apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level, the 21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, and the Juice HACCP hazard-control level, with the 2022 lead-in-juice action levels still DRAFT and therefore ineligible); and Hong Kong Cap 132V, which is the only credible instrument that writes per-form cells for carbonated beverages, tea beverages, coffee beverages, wine, tea leaf, coffee beans and named infusion botanicals. FSANZ Schedule 19 and Health Canada contribute commodity cells only. Two hard scoping rules run through the file. First, BASIS: seventeen rows split into ready-to-drink liquids certified as consumed at single strength and dry leaf, bean or powder commodities certified as sold, and the two are never mixed; each row declares a basis_guard that makes a conflation fail the build rather than ship. Second, APPLICABILITY: a stricter sovereign cell is adopted only where it actually reaches the product form, and where a stricter cell was considered and rejected the rejection is written into the cell's own substantiation rather than left for an opposing expert to discover. Where no applicable cell and no supportable near-neighbour exist, the cell is a CONTROL with mandatory lot testing and an escalation rule, and no ceiling is invented. Category 5 is regulated thinly: most rows carry numeric lead, arsenic, nickel and tin cells and controls for cadmium, mercury, aluminium and chromium, and that distribution is a fact about the law, not a gap in this build. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Beverages
_category.anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
_category.basis_family: two declared bases, never mixed: ready-to-drink liquid as consumed (wet weight, single strength, concentrates as reconstituted) and dry leaf, bean or powder commodity as sold
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.
_category.method_note: Category 5 carries two native bases and the compiler is configured never to mix them. A ready-to-drink beverage is certified in the as-consumed liquid basis at single strength, and a concentrate is assessed as reconstituted to single strength, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 already write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries. A dry leaf, dry botanical, roasted bean or beverage powder is certified in the as-sold dry-commodity basis, because that is the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples. No brewing, extraction, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction: the tea-leaf lead maximum level is never applied to a brewed cup, and a ready-to-drink beverage maximum level is never applied to a dry leaf. Where a government instrument writes the product-form split itself, HMTc preserves it rather than collapsing it: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets Tea, Green, Black at 5000 ug/kg as sold against tea beverages made from it at 200 ug/kg as consumed, and coffee beans at 500 ug/kg as sold against coffee beverages at 200 ug/kg as consumed. Two consequences of the method are disclosed rather than engineered away. The rice-based drink row is LOOSER on inorganic arsenic (30 ug/kg, EU 2023/915 section 3.4.1.6) than the juice rows (20 ug/kg, and 10 ug/kg for apple-containing juice), because the EU assessed that exact commodity and set that exact number. And several formulated-beverage rows carry a lead ceiling of 200 ug/kg because Hong Kong Cap 132V is the only credible sovereign that regulates those forms at all, while the flavoured-water row carries 5 ug/kg because the packaged-drinking-water quality standards do reach a product that is water plus flavour. Those spreads are applicability judgements, each recorded on the face of the cell, and only the endogenous Standards Ratchet in Governance Policy section 12 may lower any of them.

fruit-juices-non-apple.name: Fruit juices, non-apple
fruit-juices-non-apple.native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
fruit-juices-non-apple.scope_note: Single-strength ready-to-drink fruit juices, fruit juices from concentrate, concentrated fruit juices assessed as reconstituted, and fruit nectars, in every packaging format (carton, PET, glass, can, pouch), containing no apple juice or apple-derived juice solids. Any apple content routes the product to the apple-containing row, which carries the stricter inorganic-arsenic ceiling. Grape and berry juices sit in this row and are held to the strictest applicable cell rather than to their own looser government-written splits, which are disclosed. Rice-based and other plant-based drinks are not juices and route to the plant-milk rows; drinking water and mineral water route to Category 8; a juice carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16; an infant or young-child juice-based drink routes to Category 1.
fruit-juices-non-apple.basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
fruit-juices-non-apple.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.

Pb.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.1.19.2 sets lead in fruit juices, fruit juices from concentrate, concentrated fruit juices and fruit nectars other than those exclusively from berries and other small fruits at 30 ug/kg; Codex CXS 193 sets fruit juices at 30 ug/kg and Hong Kong Cap 132V sets the same commodity at 30 ug/kg. Three credible sovereigns converge on 30 ug/kg and the EU cell binds on jurisdiction priority.
Pb.basis_label: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice; a concentrate is assessed as reconstituted to the original juice concentration, which is the basis the instruments themselves write
Pb.substantiation: This is a direct regulatory lookup, not a calculation. The candidate set deliberately includes the looser government-written splits so the selection is auditable: grape juice at 40 ug/kg (Codex and Hong Kong) and juices exclusively from berries and other small fruits at 50 ug/kg (EU 2023/915 section 3.1.19.1 and Hong Kong), plus the older US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level of 50 ug/kg. Because the whole non-apple fruit-juice family is certified as a single row, the row ceiling is the strictest applicable value across every form in scope, 30 ug/kg. That is deliberate over-compliance for grape and berry juices relative to their own government-written cells, and it is disclosed here rather than buried: a grape or berry juice that meets 40 or 50 ug/kg is lawful in the EU, Codex and Hong Kong but is not HMTc-certifiable in this row. The US FDA 2022 draft action levels for lead in juice (10 ug/kg for single-strength apple juice, 20 ug/kg for other single-strength juices and blends) are DRAFT guidance expressly not for implementation and are therefore not eligible anchors; they are recorded so that the register's gated draft rows are visibly accounted for rather than silently omitted.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for a fruit juice. EU 2023/915's cadmium cells cover vegetables, cereals, oilseeds, pulses, cocoa and chocolate, meat, fish and mushrooms; Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Health Canada and Hong Kong Cap 132V likewise set no cadmium maximum level for fruit or for fruit juice. The nearest sovereign cadmium cells are written for vegetable commodities in a fresh-weight basis and for a different botanical family, so they are not applicable to a fruit juice. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
control.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for a fruit juice. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. The inorganic-arsenic ceiling in this row carries the health-relevant fraction. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.4.4 sets inorganic arsenic in fruit juices, concentrated fruit juices as reconstituted, and fruit nectars at 20 ug/kg, which is the strictest applicable value and binds; Health Canada's grape juice and grape nectar cell (30 ug/kg) is the looser sibling and is disclosed.
iAs.basis_label: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice (or concentrate as reconstituted)
iAs.substantiation: Direct sovereign maximum level for this exact product form and basis. The US FDA inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg is final guidance but is scoped to apple juice specifically and is not applicable to a non-apple juice row; it binds the apple-containing row instead, which is where the government wrote it. Adopting 20 ug/kg here rather than 10 is not a convenience choice: it is the refusal to extend an apple-specific instrument to commodities its issuing agency did not assess.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for a fruit juice. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a fruit juice: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 sets nickel in fruit and vegetable juices and nectars generally at 250 ug/kg and in juices and nectars from passion fruit, cocoa fruit, small fruits and berries, and coconut water at 1000 ug/kg. Both cells are named; the general cell at 250 ug/kg is the strictest applicable and binds the row.
Ni.basis_label: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid
Ni.substantiation: Direct sovereign maximum level for this exact product form, applying from 1 July 2025. Both government-written formulation bands are disclosed. As with lead, the single row ceiling is the strictest applicable across the forms in scope, so a berry or passion-fruit juice is held to 250 ug/kg rather than to its own 1000 ug/kg band; that over-compliance is stated rather than hidden. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte.

Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.basis_label: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a fruit juice. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for a fruit juice. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a single-strength fruit juice. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 3.0 to 4.0, with citric, malic and ascorbic acid present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.
not_material.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. Total chromium (Cr cell) bounds any hexavalent fraction; a Cr(VI)-specific method (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted to the liquid matrix) is reflexed where the total-chromium screen is elevated AND the finished-product pH is above 5.0, and a confirmed detection blocks certification pending a process and equipment investigation.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.

An infant or young-child apple-juice drink routes to Category 1.

The EU fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) is named and disclosed as the looser applicable alternative. The register carries the FDA instrument twice, under two ingest keys, and both are named so the duplication is visible rather than resolved silently.
iAs.basis_label: single-strength ready-to-drink juice, as consumed; a concentrate is assessed as reconstituted to single strength, the basis FDA's guidance itself specifies
iAs.substantiation: This is the government's own product-form split and HMTc preserves it: FDA assessed apple juice specifically because apple juice is a disproportionate inorganic-arsenic exposure route for young children, and it issued 10 ug/kg as final guidance rather than draft. The action level is scoped to apple juice; HMTc extends it to any blend containing apple juice, because a blend's apple fraction carries the same hazard and FDA's own guidance flags apple-containing blends as needing applicability review. That extension is a widening of scope in the strict direction within a single instrument, not a read-across to a different commodity, and it is disclosed. Occurrence data played no part in selecting 10 ug/kg.

Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 sets nickel in fruit and vegetable juices and nectars generally at 250 ug/kg; the listed band (passion fruit, cocoa fruit, small fruits and berries, coconut water) at 1000 ug/kg is disclosed. Apple juice sits in the general band, so 250 ug/kg is both the directly applicable and the strictest applicable value.
Ni.basis_label: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid
Ni.substantiation: Direct sovereign maximum level for this exact product form, applying from 1 July 2025. Where an apple-containing blend also contains a listed berry or passion-fruit juice, the row ceiling remains the strictest applicable value (250 ug/kg) rather than the blend's looser band.

The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.

A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for an apple-containing fruit juice. Pb.basis_label: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice (read across from the EU fruit-juice cell)

component_read_across.basis_label: fresh-weight edible portion of the source root or tuber vegetable, read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied
component_read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written a cadmium maximum level for vegetable juice. Three credible sovereigns converge on 100 ug/kg for the root and tuber vegetable commodity that defines this row, and that value is adopted by disclosed read-across to the juice.
component_read_across.substantiation: Root and tuber vegetables are the cadmium-relevant commodity family for this row, and EU 2023/915, Hong Kong Cap 132V and FSANZ Schedule 19 all set 100 ug/kg for it: the convergence removes any single-regulator-outlier objection. The read-across is a form change (whole root to its juice), and the basis treatment is stated precisely rather than glossed. The binding anchor eu2023_cd_root_tuber_vegetables_100 is recorded in the register on a wet-weight basis, so for the cell that actually binds there is no basis change at all. The two corroborating cells are recorded differently, Hong Kong Cap 132V as an as-sold Part 2 Schedule entry and FSANZ Schedule 19 as the portion ordinarily consumed, and each is compared to the single-strength juice at face value. No concentration, dilution or dry-matter factor is applied in either direction to any member of the candidate set. The stricter Hong Kong Cap 132V cadmium cells at 50 ug/kg were considered and are NOT adopted here, and they are named so the rejection is auditable rather than implied: cucurbit fruiting vegetables (hk_cap132v_cd_fruiting-vegetables-cucurbits_50), fruiting vegetables other than cucurbits and tomatoes (hk_cap132v_cd_fruiting-vegetables-other-than-cucurbits-and-tomatoes_50), bulb vegetables (hk_cap132v_cd_bulb-vegetables_50) and brassica vegetables other than brassica leafy vegetables (hk_cap132v_cd_brassica-vegetables-other-than-brassica-leafy-vegetable_50). Each is written for a botanical family that is not a root or tuber, while this row is defined by its root and tuber content and the same regulator wrote a separate, named root-and-tuber cell for exactly that commodity. Adopting a neighbouring family cell over the commodity own named cell would be reaching past the instrument rather than applying it. Where a blend content is predominantly bulb or brassica rather than root or tuber it is not certified in this row at all: it routes to the non-root row, whose ceiling is 50 ug/kg. Where a blend's non-root vegetable fraction predominates, the non-root row and its 50 ug/kg ceiling apply instead. Cadmium carries mandatory lot testing and Standards Ratchet surveillance under Governance Policy section 12; no occurrence data selected the number.

read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for vegetable juice. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) in the identical single-strength ready-to-drink basis, adopted by disclosed read-across.
read_across.substantiation: Arsenic reaches a root-vegetable juice through irrigation water and soil rather than through the fruit-versus-vegetable distinction, so a beverage-form arsenic cell reads across cleanly with no basis change. The US FDA apple-juice action level (10 ug/kg) was considered and rejected as inapplicable: it is scoped to a single named fruit commodity that this row excludes. The EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks cell (30 ug/kg) was considered and rejected as both looser and scoped to a rice hazard this row does not carry.

iAs.basis_label: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice (read across from the EU fruit-juice cell)

Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 writes its 250 ug/kg nickel cell for fruit AND vegetable juices and nectars generally, so this is a direct sovereign maximum level for a vegetable juice, not a read-across.
Ni.basis_label: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid
Ni.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup; the instrument names vegetable juices explicitly and applies from 1 July 2025. The listed 1000 ug/kg band is written for passion fruit, cocoa fruit, small fruits and berries and coconut water, none of which is a vegetable juice, so it is not applicable to this row. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte.

tAs.screen_note: Total arsenic is recorded as a SCREEN and not as a protective standalone ceiling. The health-relevant species in this product form is inorganic arsenic, which this row caps at 20 ug/kg; a total-arsenic value twenty-five times higher cannot be protective on its own, and it is published because a credible sovereign wrote a total-arsenic maximum level for the source commodity, not because it describes a safe level. The binding health control in this row is the inorganic-arsenic cell together with the speciation reflex recorded below.

read_across.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 2 sets arsenic, expressed as total arsenic, in vegetables at 500 ug/kg. No credible sovereign has written an unspeciated arsenic maximum level for vegetable juice itself, so the source-commodity cell is adopted by disclosed read-across from the same instrument and on the same logic as this row's cadmium anchor, and it is recorded as a screen.
read_across.substantiation: The candidate set and the rejections. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg), and the unspeciated beverage arsenic values that exist sit in the packaged-water schedules (US 21 CFR 165.110 and Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, both 10 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments. Adopting the Hong Kong vegetable cell publishes a sovereign ceiling where this row previously published none, and it loosens nothing: the 20 ug/kg inorganic-arsenic ceiling and the speciation reflex continue to bind, so no lot that would have failed under the previous control disposition can pass under this one. No occurrence data selected the number.

tAs.basis_label: fresh-weight edible portion of the source vegetable (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule, which the register records as an as-sold commodity cell), read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied; total arsenic

Species never substitute for totals and totals never substitute for species: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement, and compliance with the 500 ug/kg total-arsenic screen does not satisfy the inorganic-arsenic ceiling.

read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written a total-mercury maximum level for vegetable juice itself, but Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 12 sets mercury, expressed as total mercury, in vegetables other than edible fungi at 10 ug/kg, and that is the source-commodity cell for a root-vegetable-containing juice. Adopting the Hong Kong vegetable cell publishes a sovereign ceiling where this row previously published none, and it removes nothing: total mercury remains a mandatory lot test and the escalation rule below continues to bind. No occurrence data selected the number; the number is Hong Kong's, unchanged.

tHg.basis_label: fresh-weight edible portion of the source vegetable (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule, which the register records as an as-sold commodity cell), read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied; total mercury

not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. Cr.basis_label: fresh-weight edible portion of the source vegetable (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule, which the register records as an as-sold commodity cell), read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied; total chromium
Cr.binding_control: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot and reported on the certificate. A result above 250 ug/kg, which is 50 percent of the screen value, or any result that departs materially from the applicant's documented process baseline, triggers the Cr(VI) reflex defined in the Cr-VI cell of this row together with an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a root-vegetable-containing juice. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.
not_material.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (Hong Kong Cap 132V vegetables other than pulses 500 ug/kg, which is this row's total-chromium screen; US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.

plant-milks-non-soy-non-rice.name: Plant milks, non-soy non-rice

plant-milks-non-soy-non-rice.scope_note: Ready-to-drink plant-based milk alternatives made from a base other than soy or rice: almond, oat, cashew, coconut, hemp, pea, macadamia, walnut, flax and blends of those. Includes shelf-stable and refrigerated formats and canned coconut milk sold as a beverage. Soy-based drinks route to the soy row (a distinct nickel and aluminium accumulation profile); any rice content routes the product to the rice-based row and its dedicated EU inorganic-arsenic cell. A plant-based infant formula routes to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule; a plant-based drink carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16; culinary canned coconut milk sold as an ingredient rather than a beverage routes to the pantry categories.

plant-milks-non-soy-non-rice.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.

read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for a plant-based drink. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the Hong Kong Cap 132V lead cell for Milk (20 ug/kg, as consumed), the dairy beverage this product form substitutes for and shares a serving format, consumption pattern and liquid as-consumed basis with. It is adopted by disclosed read-across.
read_across.substantiation: A almond, oat, cashew, coconut, hemp or pea drink is not milk, and this is stated rather than glossed: the read-across rests on form and use, not on composition. The candidate set was the sovereign cells reachable in the same as-consumed liquid basis: the Hong Kong milk cell (20 ug/kg), the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg, a juice this product is not), and the Hong Kong carbonated-beverage cell (200 ug/kg, a carbonation form this product does not take). The milk cell is both the nearest by form and use and the strictest of those three, so no convenience selection is available among them. The packaged-drinking-water quality standards are stricter still (US 21 CFR 165.110 lead at 5 ug/kg, Hong Kong packaged drinking water at 10 ug/kg) and were considered and rejected on applicability: they govern water sold as water, they are Category 8 instruments under the taxonomy boundary rule, and a plant-based drink is an opaque formulated beverage carrying several percent suspended and dissolved plant solids plus mineral fortificants, which is not the matrix those standards were written for. The row's nut, oat and seed bases are grown in soils whose lead burden varies by origin, which is why lead is a mandatory lot test and a Standards Ratchet surveillance analyte here rather than a formality. The dry-commodity lead cells for the source seed, grain or nut are written in an as-sold dry basis and are deliberately NOT applied to the liquid drink; converting between them would require an invented dilution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to the infant-formula 8:1 reconstitution and forbids elsewhere.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a rice-based plant drink. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant. Plant-based drinks additionally carry mineral-fortification premixes and stabiliser systems, so an aluminium result is investigated against the fortificant and stabiliser specifications as well as the packaging.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for a rice-based plant drink. control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: a plant-based drink is near-neutral (typically pH 6.5 to 7.5) and low in the organic acids and ascorbate that drive Cr(VI) reduction in an acidic beverage, so the reduction cannot be assumed. flavored-waters.name: Flavored waters
flavored-waters.native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
flavored-waters.scope_note: Packaged still and sparkling waters carrying added flavour, essence or a trace of fruit essence, sold as water with flavour and containing no meaningful nutritive or functional load: no added sugar or sugar-substitute sweetener system beyond a trace, no electrolyte or stimulant formulation, no juice declared as an ingredient at a level that makes the product a juice drink. Products that carry a formulated load (sweetener, electrolyte, caffeine, botanical extract, protein, added juice) are NOT flavoured waters for this purpose and route to the sports and energy drink row or the soft-drink row, because the water-law anchor family used here rests on the product being water plus flavour. Plain bottled drinking water and natural mineral water route to Category 8 by the taxonomy boundary rule; a flavoured water with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16. This row's anchor family is the PACKAGED-DRINKING-WATER food law (US 21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards and the Hong Kong Cap 132V bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters schedule), not the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels. US EPA and Health Canada drinking-water MCLs are water-utility instruments that regulate a distribution system rather than a packaged food, they belong to Category 8, and they are deliberately outside this row's audit scope and candidate set; where one of them is stricter than the value adopted here (Health Canada total mercury at 1 ug/L, for example) that is disclosed rather than adopted, because a utility-facing MCL is not a maximum level for a packaged beverage.
flavored-waters.audit_scope: bottled water|bottled drinking water|bottled or packaged drinking water|carbonated beverage
flavored-waters.basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
flavored-waters.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction. Within that, this row's anchors are all packaged-drinking-water quality standards in a per-litre aqueous basis, which converts to ug/kg at 1 mg/L = 1000 ug/kg for a beverage of unit density; the register already carries the converted values and no further treatment is applied.

read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for flavoured water specifically. read_across.substantiation: A flavoured water is, compositionally, packaged drinking water plus a flavour dose, and it is sold and consumed as water; the packaged-water quality standard is therefore the nearest applicable sovereign cell in an identical aqueous as-consumed basis. The competing candidate was the Hong Kong carbonated-beverage lead cell (200 ug/kg), which does directly cover a sparkling flavoured water as a carbonated beverage. Both are applicable to forms in this row, so Method v2.0 step 3 compels the strictest applicable value, and that is 5 ug/kg, not 200. Adopting 200 here would have been the convenience choice and is expressly rejected: a product that is 99 percent water cannot be held to a ceiling forty times the standard its own water base must already meet. The scope note draws the boundary that makes this defensible, excluding formulated beverages from the row.

Pb.basis_label: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the US bottled-water quality standard)

read_across.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets cadmium in bottled or packaged drinking waters other than natural mineral waters at 3 ug/kg; it is the strictest applicable packaged-water cadmium cell and is adopted by disclosed read-across. The US 21 CFR 165.110 value (5 ug/kg) is disclosed as the looser sibling.
read_across.substantiation: Same anchor family and same reasoning as the lead cell: a flavoured water is water plus flavour, the packaged-water food law is the nearest applicable sovereign cell, and the strictest of the two applicable packaged-water values is taken. This is the only row in Category 5 that carries a numeric cadmium ceiling; every other row is a cadmium control, because no sovereign writes cadmium cells for juices, plant drinks, soft drinks, tea, coffee or infusions.

Cd.basis_label: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the Hong Kong packaged-water cell)

read_across.label: US 21 CFR 165.110 sets arsenic in bottled water at 10 ug/kg without speciation, and Hong Kong Cap 132V sets total arsenic in packaged drinking water at the same 10 ug/kg. Two credible sovereigns converge; the value is adopted by disclosed read-across as a TOTAL-arsenic ceiling.
read_across.substantiation: This is the one place in the category where a sovereign writes an unspeciated arsenic limit for a beverage, and it is taken as written: a total, not a species. Because the total is capped at 10 ug/kg, the inorganic fraction is bounded by it (iAs <= tAs), which is why the inorganic-arsenic cell in this row is a control rather than a separate looser number. Public-water-system MCLs (US EPA and Health Canada, both 10 ug/L) are not used as anchors here for the reason given in the scope note, though they carry the same value.

tAs.basis_label: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage, total arsenic (read across from the US bottled-water standard)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a packaged water or a flavoured water; the packaged-water instruments cap arsenic as an unspeciated total, and this row adopts that total at 10 ug/kg. Publishing a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would either duplicate the total (adding nothing) or exceed it (an impossibility, since iAs <= tAs by identity), so the honest disposition is a control bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling rather than an invented species number. This is a control and not a not-material determination because inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant species in an aqueous matrix and is genuinely present in groundwater-sourced water: the analyte is real, only the separate ceiling is unavailable.
control.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed on every lot whose total arsenic exceeds 5 ug/kg (50 percent of the total-arsenic ceiling), and on every source-water change. read_across.substantiation: Same anchor family as the lead, cadmium and arsenic cells in this row. read_across.substantiation: The candidate set and why each alternative was rejected. The audit scan flags the whole juice and nectar lead family as stricter and unselected: the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg), the Codex and Hong Kong grape-juice cells (40 ug/kg), the EU and Hong Kong berry and small-fruit juice cells (50 ug/kg) and the US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level (50 ug/kg). control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for a sports or energy drink. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
control.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for a sports or energy drink.
