matcha.name: Matcha
matcha.native_basis_label: dry powder as sold, reported on the as-sold article; matcha is whisked into water and ingested in its entirety, so the as-sold powder basis is also the basis in which the consumer's whole dose is delivered
matcha.scope_note: Stone-ground Camellia sinensis leaf powder (matcha, and culinary-grade matcha sold for beverage preparation), including matcha-based latte and drink powders whose matcha content is the dominant characterising ingredient. Split out from the true-tea row for one mechanistic reason that changes the exposure arithmetic rather than the number: matcha is suspended and swallowed whole, so the entire contaminant load of the leaf is ingested, whereas an infused leaf transfers only the extractable fraction and is discarded. The published ceiling is the same government value that binds tea leaf, because that is the only sovereign value for the commodity; the difference is that in this row it is a whole-dose ceiling, which is disclosed on the aluminium and lead cells. A matcha product with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16; a sweetened matcha drink mix whose dominant ingredient is sugar or dairy solids routes to the cocoa-and-malted-beverage-mix row's basis treatment by analogy and is certified there.
matcha.basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight
matcha.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard.

Pb.label: Matcha is green tea, so Hong Kong Cap 132V's Tea, Green, Black lead cell (5000 ug/kg, as sold) is a DIRECT sovereign maximum level for this product form and basis, not a read-across. It is the only credible sovereign lead value for the commodity and it binds.
Pb.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup: matcha is Camellia sinensis leaf, ground rather than left whole, and no credible instrument writes a separate cell for the ground form, so the commodity cell applies as written. The consequence is disclosed rather than smoothed: because matcha is ingested whole, a lot at the 5000 ug/kg ceiling delivers the full leaf lead burden to the consumer, where an infusion made from leaf at the same ceiling would deliver only the extractable fraction and Hong Kong's own beverage cell would cap the resulting drink at 200 ug/kg. HMTc does not resolve that asymmetry by inventing an extraction-corrected number, which Method v2.0 forbids; it publishes the government value, flags the whole-leaf ingestion route on the certificate, and treats this cell as a first-order Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12, where certified-lot evidence is the only admissible basis for a lower value.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for matcha powder. No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for tea in any form. As with lead, the whole-leaf ingestion route makes this a live cell rather than a formality, and the absence of a sovereign ceiling is disclosed rather than filled. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
control.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for matcha powder. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. No sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic cell for tea in any form, so both arsenic cells in this row are controls and the escalation rule carries the obligation. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for matcha powder. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell is scoped either to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to packaged and public drinking water. None of those is applicable to this dry commodity, and applying a ready-to-drink beverage cell to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation. Inorganic arsenic is a Tier-1 analyte, so it is speciated whenever the total-arsenic screen is elevated.
control.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot exceeds 100 ug/kg in the as-sold dry basis; a confirmed inorganic-arsenic result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for matcha powder. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in dry matcha powder: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for matcha powder. EU 2024/1987 is the only comprehensive sovereign nickel instrument; its cells cover cereals, pulses, oilseeds, tree nuts, vegetables, cocoa and chocolate, infant formula, baby food and fruit and vegetable juices, and none of them covers this commodity. The juice and nectar cell (250 ug/kg) is written in a ready-to-drink basis and cannot be applied to a dry commodity, and the dry-commodity cells that do exist are written for other plant families. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte on the mandatory eight-total panel.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. An elevated result escalates to a soil, cultivar and stainless-equipment investigation.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a tin maximum level for dry matcha powder. The exclusion is written into the instrument itself: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5 scopes its inorganic-tin maximum levels to canned beverages and canned foods and expressly excepts canned dried and canned powdered products, and the Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong canned-food cells carry the same carve-out. There is therefore no sovereign number for a dry beverage commodity and no supportable read-across, because the canned-liquid cells are written in a ready-to-drink basis. Tin is nonetheless on the mandatory eight-total panel.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. Where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink form of this product, that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin maximum level in the as-consumed basis.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for matcha powder, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable: the only sovereign aluminium values are packaged-drinking-water quality standards written in a litre-of-water basis (Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1). Applying a water-basis value to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation of roughly three orders of magnitude. Aluminium is the highest-priority control in this row. Camellia sinensis is an aluminium hyperaccumulator, and matcha delivers the whole leaf rather than an infusion, so the aluminium the leaf accumulated is ingested in full rather than partially extracted. No credible sovereign has written a ceiling for tea in any form. HMTc mandates aluminium on every certified lot, reports it on the certificate with the whole-leaf ingestion route stated, and declines to invent a number; the analyte is a first-order Standards Ratchet surveillance priority.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for matcha powder. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: this row's certified article is a DRY powder, so there is no aqueous matrix in which Cr(VI) could be reduced to Cr(III), and the acidic-beverage reduction argument is unavailable. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.

coffee.name: Coffee
coffee.native_basis_label: dry commodity as sold (green beans, roasted whole beans, ground coffee, coffee pods and capsules assessed on their coffee fill, instant coffee solids), reported on the as-sold article; this is the lot the applicant packages and the auditor samples
coffee.scope_note: Coffee as a dry commodity: green and roasted Coffea arabica and canephora beans, ground coffee, single-serve pods and capsules assessed on the coffee fill rather than the hardware, and instant or freeze-dried coffee solids. A mushroom coffee or any coffee carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16 by the taxonomy boundary rule. Coffee-flavoured dairy and plant beverages route to Category 24 or the plant-milk rows respectively. Hong Kong Cap 132V writes the product-form split for this commodity itself, setting Coffee beans at 500 ug/kg lead in the as-sold basis and Coffee beverages at 200 ug/kg in the as-consumed basis under its Note 11; HMTc preserves the split. An applicant selling canned or bottled ready-to-drink coffee is assessed on that product form in the as-consumed liquid basis against the 200 ug/kg beverage cell; an applicant selling beans, grounds, pods or instant solids is assessed in this row's dry basis. Neither number is converted into the other basis, and no brew-strength or extraction factor is invented in either direction. The capsule or pod hardware itself is a food-contact article and is governed by Category 9, not here.
coffee.basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight
coffee.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard.

Pb.label: Lead 500 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign coffee maximum level in the as-sold dry basis, set concurrently by Hong Kong Cap 132V (coffee beans, 0.5 mg/kg), MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (roasted coffee beans and powder, 0.5 mg/kg) and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 (the identical MERCOSUR transposition). A single coffee row certifies every dry form against this strictest applicable value.
Pb.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. Three sovereigns converge on 500 ug/kg for the roasted bean and powder on the as-sold basis, and HMTc applies that ceiling across the dry coffee forms in scope (green bean, roasted bean, ground, pod fill, instant solids), because roasting and grinding are physical transformations of the same commodity that do not add lead and instant solids concentrate the extractable fraction of a bean already held to this ceiling. That single-commodity extension is disclosed, and it over-complies relative to the looser government-written soluble-coffee cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay both 1000 ug/kg), Singapore coffee beans (2000) and Vietnam coffee (2000), each recorded here rather than buried. The Thailand residual food-other lead cell (1000, as-sold) also legally reaches coffee but is looser and is surveyed, not selected. China GB 2762-2022 is register-verified to exclude raw and roasted coffee beans from its nuts-and-seeds lead cell, so it sets no coffee lead limit. Hong Kong caps the resulting ready-to-drink coffee beverage at 200 ug/kg as consumed; that product-form split is preserved rather than collapsed into this dry-commodity row. Occurrence data played no part.

Cd.label: Cadmium 100 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign coffee maximum level in the as-sold dry basis, set by MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (roasted coffee beans and powder, 0.1 mg/kg) and its identical Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 transposition.
Cd.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. The roasted bean and powder cadmium cell at 100 ug/kg is the strictest admissible as-sold coffee value and binds the harmonized dry row, over-complying relative to the government-written soluble-coffee cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay both 200) and Vietnam coffee (1000). No general as-sold cadmium cell in the register is stricter: Singapore other-food and Uruguay solid-foods both sit at 200. The EU, Codex, FSANZ and Health Canada set no cadmium maximum level for coffee in any form. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

tAs.label: Total arsenic 200 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign coffee maximum level in the as-sold dry basis, set by MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (roasted coffee beans and powder, 0.2 mg/kg) and its identical Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 transposition. It also serves as the enforceable parent ceiling for the inorganic-arsenic species bound.
tAs.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. The MERCOSUR and Paraguay total-arsenic roasted bean and powder cell at 200 ug/kg is the strictest admissible as-sold coffee value and binds the harmonized row, over-complying relative to the soluble-coffee cells (both 500), Singapore coffee beans (1000), Vietnam coffee (1000) and the Thailand residual food-other total-arsenic cell (2000). The regulators that write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU fruit juices, US FDA apple juice) do not reach coffee. Total arsenic is the parent screen that gates reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

subsumed.rationale: No sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for coffee, and coffee is not a defining-inorganic-arsenic-pathway matrix carrying a species-only limit (unlike rice or apple juice). Under the Certification-Readiness Ruling's species-bounding clause, inorganic arsenic is a component of total arsenic bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling adjudicated for this row (iAs <= tAs = 200 ug/kg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell or a fabricated number.
subsumed.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot reaches the trigger min(species limit, 50 percent of the total-arsenic ceiling); a confirmed result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.
subsumed.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic cell for coffee. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic limit is scoped to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to drinking water. Inorganic arsenic is a component of and bounded by total arsenic, which this row governs directly.
subsumed.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA (apple-juice action level, Closer to Zero); FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Singapore Food Regulations; Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011; Thailand MOPH 414/2020 — none sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for coffee.
subsumed.substantiation: Bounded by the total-arsenic cell (tAs = 200 ug/kg). Enforced by reflex speciation; not a routine per-lot species assay for this form.

tHg.label: Total mercury 20 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level reaching coffee in the as-sold basis, set by Thailand MOPH Notification 414/2020 as the residual mercury cell for foods other than the listed mercury categories (0.02 mg/kg). Thailand sets no coffee-specific mercury cell, so coffee falls under this residual, which is stricter than and supersedes the looser coffee-specific Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 value (50 ug/kg).
tHg.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup, register-verified. Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level, and an already-admitted residual food-other total-mercury cell (Thailand MOPH 414/2020, as-sold) legally reaches dry coffee on the native basis and is stricter (20) than the Vietnam coffee-specific cell (50). If the Vietnam coffee cell is admissible then so is the Thailand food-other cell, and the stricter of the two binds. Singapore other-food and Uruguay foods-general both sit at 50 and are disclosed as looser. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in the coffee supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel and is measured every lot. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

subsumed.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in dry coffee: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury ceiling adjudicated for this row (20 ug/kg); no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
subsumed.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg = 20 ug/kg). Methylmercury speciation is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine per-lot test for this form.
subsumed.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury, which this row governs directly.
subsumed.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap 132V; MERCOSUR; Paraguay; Vietnam; Thailand — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.
subsumed.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg = 20 ug/kg). Enforced by reflex speciation.

read_across.label: Nickel 15000 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from EU 2024/1987, which sets nickel in cocoa powder and fat-reduced cocoa powder (drinking chocolate) at 15 mg/kg. No sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for coffee; cocoa is the nearest applicable regulated commodity.
read_across.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign regulates nickel in coffee. The nearest applicable sovereign cell is EU 2024/1987's cocoa-powder nickel limit (15000 ug/kg), and the analogy is agronomic rather than merely botanical: coffee and cocoa are the roasted seeds of tropical tree crops grown on acidic tropical soils that mobilise plant-available nickel, prepared and consumed as beverages, and cocoa powder is the closest processed analog to instant coffee solids. The EU assessed cocoa and set 15000 but did not assess coffee, so this value is applied by disclosed read-across and never presented as a coffee-specific government limit. The ceiling is a conservative backstop well above typical measured coffee nickel; nickel is a Tier-2 analyte measured every lot, and an elevated result escalates to a soil, cultivar and stainless-equipment investigation.

Sn.label: Tin 250000 ug/kg is set by the general food catch-all cells that legally reach coffee in the as-sold basis: Singapore Food Regulations Regulation 31(4) (any food, 250 ppm) and the Uruguay RBN foods-in-general cell (250 mg/kg). No sovereign writes a coffee-specific or dry-beverage-commodity tin cell; the canned and tinplate tin limits are container-migration cells in a different basis and are firewalled out of this dry row.
Sn.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup against the general as-sold food catch-alls. Every product-specific tin limit in the register is a canned or tinplate container-migration cell written in a ready-to-drink or wet basis (the EU, Codex, MERCOSUR and Vietnam canned-beverage and canned-food cells, 100000 to 250000), and each excludes dried and powdered products by its own text; applying any of them to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation. The only sovereign tin numbers that reach dry coffee as sold are the general food catch-alls, which converge on 250000. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte with no raw-material source in coffee; an elevated result is a packaging-integrity signal, and where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink coffee that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin cell in the as-consumed basis. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for coffee, and no analogous dry-food aluminium contaminant cell exists: the only sovereign aluminium values are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (a litre-of-water basis, Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1), neither of which is applicable to a dry commodity, and Method v2.0 forbids deriving a ceiling from occurrence data. Aluminium nonetheless carries a real exposure pathway here (acidic tropical soils mobilise plant-available aluminium, and single-serve capsules are predominantly aluminium), so under the Certification-Readiness Ruling this cell is a baseline-monitor screen rather than a not-material determination. It is the one cell on this panel that cannot yet resolve to a firm limit-of-record: a testable numeric baseline of the form '< X ug/kg by ICP-MS' requires the accredited laboratory's documented method reporting limit, which is not yet in the register. Until that number is recorded the cell is a mandatory-monitored control and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis, established as a baseline-monitor limit-of-record at the laboratory's documented reporting limit once provided. A result that departs materially from the applicant's documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar, capsule-packaging and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire pending a documented method limit of quantification, not an invented numeric standard.

read_across.label: Total chromium 1000 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from China GB 2762-2022, which sets total chromium uniformly at 1.0 mg/kg across its dry plant-food commodity classes (grains and grain products; beans, bean products and legumes). No sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for coffee; China GB 2762 is an already-admitted, live-cited HMTc anchor and the nearest applicable dry-plant-commodity instrument.
read_across.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign regulates total chromium in coffee. China GB 2762-2022 sets a uniform total-chromium level of 1000 ug/kg across its dry plant-food commodity classes, and coffee is a dry plant-derived food commodity read across to that uniform level. Coffee is not itself a grain or a legume (it is the roasted seed of a tropical drupe), so the value is applied as a general dry-plant-commodity read-across rather than by claiming coffee into either China GB class; both the grains cell and the beans-and-legumes cell (identical at 1000) are named so the selection is auditable. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-equipment and process-water leaching screen; the health-relevant species is governed in the Cr-VI cell. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

subsumed.rationale: No sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic aqueous beverage is unavailable here: this row's certified article is a dry bean, ground or solid with no aqueous phase in which Cr(VI) could reduce to Cr(III). Cr(VI) is a component of total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr) and is bounded by the total-chromium ceiling adjudicated for this row (1000 ug/kg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
subsumed.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS every lot; Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) reflexed whenever total chromium reaches the trigger min(species limit, 50 percent of the total-chromium ceiling). A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
subsumed.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage. Cr(VI) is a component of and bounded by total chromium, which this row governs by read-across.
subsumed.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ; Health Canada; China GB 2762-2022; Hong Kong Cap 132V — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.
subsumed.substantiation: Bounded by the total-chromium cell (Cr = 1000 ug/kg). Enforced by reflex speciation.

coffee.sovereign_admission_note: Coffee is regulated for heavy metals almost entirely outside the EU/Codex/US/FSANZ/Health Canada core set. This row therefore anchors its numeric cells on the coffee-specific and general-food maximum levels of MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011, Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, Thailand MOPH Notification 414/2020, Singapore Food Regulations, Uruguay RBN and China GB 2762-2022 — national and regional food-contaminant instruments already primary-verified in the register and, for Hong Kong Cap 132V and China GB 2762, already admitted and cited across shipped HMTc categories. Each anchor is named by its register id and disclosed on the face of the cell; none is occurrence-derived. Whether to formalise this widened sovereign-anchor set program-wide (config _category.credible) is a separate governance decision logged for review.

soft-drinks-carbonated-beverages.name: Soft drinks/carbonated beverages
soft-drinks-carbonated-beverages.native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
soft-drinks-carbonated-beverages.scope_note: Ready-to-drink carbonated and still soft drinks: colas, lemon-lime and other flavoured carbonates, root beer, ginger ale, tonic water, bitter lemon, sodas containing a minor juice fraction, and their post-mix syrup and concentrate forms assessed as dispensed or reconstituted to the label dilution. Every packaging format including aluminium cans, PET, glass and post-mix bag-in-box. A carbonated water with no formulated load routes to the flavoured-water row; a sports, isotonic or energy formulation routes to the sports and energy drink row; a fruit juice or nectar routes to the juice rows; a fermented soft drink routes to the fermented-beverage row. This row is a FORMULATED ready-to-drink beverage, not water with flavour: the packaged-drinking-water quality standards relied on for the flavoured-water row are not applicable here, because the product carries a substantial dissolved load (sweetener systems, electrolyte salts, acidulants, stimulants, botanical extracts, colours and juice concentrates) that those instruments do not contemplate. The boundary is stated so the difference in published ceilings between this row and the flavoured-water row is legible as an applicability judgement rather than an inconsistency.
soft-drinks-carbonated-beverages.basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
soft-drinks-carbonated-beverages.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. read_across.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 9 sets lead in Carbonated beverages at 0.2 mg/kg = 200 ug/kg, with Note 11 scoping the cell to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink. That cell directly governs the carbonated forms in this row and is the nearest applicable sovereign value for the still soft drinks the row also admits, which share the formulation, the process and the packaging but not the carbonation. It is adopted by disclosed read-across so that a single ceiling governs both forms.
read_across.substantiation: The provenance is recorded as read-across and not as regulatory-alignment because this row's scope is wider than the instrument's. For a cola, a tonic water or a ginger ale the Hong Kong cell is a direct sovereign maximum level for the exact product form; for a still soft drink it is the nearest applicable analog, and the tag follows the weaker of the two rather than the stronger. The sibling sports and energy drink row adopts the same anchor for the same still and carbonated mix and carries the same tag, so the two rows are consistent on their face. Three disclosures belong here. First, no other credible sovereign regulates this product form at all: the EU, Codex, FSANZ and Health Canada write no soft-drink lead cell, so 200 ug/kg is the whole of the applicable law and there is no stricter applicable value to select. Second, the stricter beverage cells that exist are inapplicable and were rejected as such rather than quietly ignored: the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg) are scoped to fruit juices, juices from concentrate and nectars, which a cola carrying a few percent juice is not, and the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (5 to 10 ug/kg) govern water sold as water. HMTc will not reach past an instrument's scope to publish a better-looking number. Third, HMTc does not pretend 200 ug/kg is a strong ceiling: this cell is a declared Standards Ratchet priority, and Governance Policy section 12 is the only route by which certified-lot evidence may lower it.

Wine, cider, perry and beer are OUT of this row's scope and are not certifiable under it; they are held in development. The reason is stated plainly because it is a limitation and not a boundary of convenience: the only credible-set lead value this register carries for any of those four forms is the Hong Kong Cap 132V Wine cell (hk_cap132v_pb_wine_200), and the EU 2023/915 wine, cider, perry and fruit-wine lead cells are absent from the register. Selecting a strictest applicable value out of a pool that is known to be missing an instrument is not an execution of the government-limit-only method, so no ceiling is published for those forms. The absence is logged as a register gap; when those cells are ingested through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway the row is recompiled and the four forms are admitted against the strictest applicable value rather than against the residue of an incomplete pool. Dairy kefir and other cultured dairy drinks route to Category 24; kombucha and any tea-substrate ferment route to the kombucha row; a fermented drink carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16. The row's distinctive hazard is process rather than agronomic: fermentation drives the matrix to pH 2.5 to 3.8 and holds it there for days to weeks in contact with vessels, seals, taps and tubing, which makes equipment leaching a first-order route for lead, nickel and chromium, and that is why the lot-testing and escalation obligations in the control cells are written around equipment and not only around ingredients.

read_across.substantiation: The candidate set and the rejections, stated plainly because this is the cell most open to attack. The audit scan flags the entire juice and nectar lead family as stricter and unselected: the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg), the Hong Kong grape-juice cell (40 ug/kg), the EU and Hong Kong berry and small-fruit juice cells (50 ug/kg) and the US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level (50 ug/kg). All were considered and all are rejected on the same two grounds: a finished ferment is not a fruit juice, a juice from concentrate or a nectar within those instruments' scope, and fermentation is precisely the step that changes the matrix and opens the equipment-leaching route, so an unfermented-input cell does not describe the certified product. The packaged-drinking-water standards (5 to 10 ug/kg) govern water sold as water. That leaves the Wine cell, which is a genuine sovereign value for a fermented fruit beverage in the identical as-consumed basis. HMTc adopts it for the ferments this row certifies and does not conceal two things about it. It is weak: because the acid ferment sits against equipment for weeks, this cell carries mandatory lot testing with an equipment and closure investigation on any result above 30 ug/kg, and it is a declared Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12. And it is drawn from a pool the register is known to be missing entries from: the EU 2023/915 wine, cider, perry and fruit-wine lead cells are not in the register, their absence is logged as a register gap, and it is filled neither by an occurrence value nor by recollection of the instrument. That gap is why wine, cider, perry and beer are excluded from this row's scope rather than certified against 200 ug/kg, and it also qualifies this read-across for the forms that remain: if any of the missing cells is stricter than 200 ug/kg it becomes the nearest applicable sovereign value for a fermented beverage and supersedes this anchor at the next recompilation. Until then the read-across is published with that qualification on its face rather than as a settled ceiling.

not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.

kombucha-tea-based.name: Kombucha, tea-based
kombucha-tea-based.native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
kombucha-tea-based.scope_note: Ready-to-drink kombucha and other tea-substrate ferments: sweetened Camellia sinensis or herbal-infusion base fermented with a bacterial and yeast consortium, with or without added juice, botanicals or carbonation, in bottle, can and keg formats. Non-tea ferments route to the fermented-beverage row; dairy ferments route to Category 24; a kombucha carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16. The row sits at the intersection of two hazard routes and both are carried in the control cells: the tea substrate brings the leaf's accumulated aluminium and lead into the liquid through extraction, and the ferment then holds a pH 2.5 to 3.5 matrix against vessels, seals and taps for one to three weeks, which is a live equipment-leaching condition. This row is certified in the as-consumed liquid basis; the dry tea leaf used as substrate is a separate product form certified in the true-tea row's as-sold basis, and no extraction factor is invented to convert between the two.
kombucha-tea-based.basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
kombucha-tea-based.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.

read_across.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets lead in Tea beverages made from Tea, Green, Black at 0.2 mg/kg = 200 ug/kg, with Note 11 scoping the cell to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink. Kombucha is a ready-to-drink beverage made from tea, so this is the nearest applicable sovereign value and arguably a direct cell; it is recorded as a disclosed read-across because the instrument does not name the fermented form.
read_across.substantiation: The read-across is conservative in its own framing: it is recorded as a read-across rather than claimed as direct regulatory alignment, because fermentation is a real transformation the Hong Kong schedule does not address, and overclaiming the provenance tag would be the kind of small dishonesty an opposing expert is paid to find. The alternatives were considered and rejected: the EU and Codex fruit-juice cells (30 ug/kg) are scoped to juices and nectars, which kombucha is not, even when juice is added post-ferment; the Hong Kong Wine cell (200 ug/kg) is the same value by a less apt route; the dry tea-leaf cell (5000 ug/kg) is in the wrong basis and would be absurd applied to a liquid. The 200 ug/kg value is weak relative to the leaching and extraction routes this product has, so the cell carries mandatory lot testing with an equipment, closure and substrate investigation on any result above 30 ug/kg, and it is a declared Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12.

Pb.basis_label: as consumed, ready-to-drink tea-based beverage (read across from the Hong Kong tea-beverage cell)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for kombucha or another tea-substrate ferment. No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for tea, for a tea beverage, or for any fermented beverage. Hong Kong Cap 132V names tea and tea beverages for lead but not for cadmium, and the EU, Codex, FSANZ and Health Canada set no cell for either form. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
control.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for kombucha or another tea-substrate ferment. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. The inorganic-arsenic cell in this row carries the health-relevant fraction. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a tea beverage or a fermented beverage. The EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) is the strictest sovereign inorganic-arsenic value for any ready-to-drink beverage and is adopted by disclosed read-across in the identical liquid basis.
read_across.substantiation: Beverage-to-beverage read-across with no basis change, adopted in the strict direction because no instrument covers this form. Arsenic arrives with the brewing water, the tea substrate and any added juice or botanical, all routes an aqueous beverage cell at 20 ug/kg contemplates.

iAs.basis_label: wet weight, ready-to-drink beverage (read across from the EU fruit-juice inorganic-arsenic cell)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for kombucha or another tea-substrate ferment. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a tea-based fermented beverage: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

read_across.label: No credible sovereign has written a nickel maximum level for a tea beverage or a fermented beverage. EU 2024/1987's fruit and vegetable juices and nectars cell (250 ug/kg) is the only sovereign nickel value written for a ready-to-drink beverage and is adopted by disclosed read-across in the identical liquid basis.
read_across.substantiation: Beverage-to-beverage read-across with no basis change. As in the non-tea fermented row, a low-pH ferment held for one to three weeks against stainless vessels, welds and taps is a live nickel leaching condition, so the control obligation is written around equipment qualification as well as ingredients. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte and a declared Standards Ratchet surveillance priority here.

Ni.basis_label: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink beverage (read across from the EU beverage nickel cell)

Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.basis_label: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for kombucha or another tea-substrate ferment. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant. Aluminium is the highest-priority control in this row and for a reason specific to it: Camellia sinensis is an aluminium hyperaccumulator, a meaningful fraction of leaf aluminium is extracted into a hot-water infusion, and the resulting liquid is then acidified by fermentation and often packaged in aluminium cans. No credible sovereign sets an aluminium ceiling for tea, for a tea beverage or for a fermented beverage, so the analyte is mandatory on every certified lot, reported on the certificate, and declared a Standards Ratchet surveillance priority; no number is invented.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for kombucha or another tea-substrate ferment. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in kombucha or another tea-substrate ferment. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 2.5 to 3.5 after fermentation, with acetic, gluconic and lactic acid, residual sugars and tea polyphenols present, the polyphenols themselves being strong Cr(VI) reductants) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.
not_material.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. Total chromium (Cr cell) bounds any hexavalent fraction; a Cr(VI)-specific method (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted to the liquid matrix) is reflexed where the total-chromium screen is elevated AND the finished-product pH is above 5.0, and a confirmed detection blocks certification pending a process and equipment investigation.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.

cocoa-beverage-mixes.name: Cocoa/hot-chocolate beverage mixes and malted drink powders
cocoa-beverage-mixes.native_basis_label: dry powder as sold, reported on the as-sold article, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 use for the cocoa-powder cells that bind this row (product as placed on the market)
cocoa-beverage-mixes.cross_reference: Appended to Category 5 to resolve the dangling Category 33 cross-reference. Chocolate confectionery and eating chocolate are NOT in this row: they are a different product form with their own government-written cocoa-solids bands, and they route to the confectionery category.
cocoa-beverage-mixes.scope_note: Dry powders sold to be reconstituted into a beverage: unsweetened cocoa powder sold for drinking, sweetened cocoa powder, powdered drinking chocolate and hot-chocolate mixes, and malted drink powders whose characterising ingredient is cocoa or malt. Includes fat-reduced cocoa powder. Excludes eating chocolate and chocolate confectionery, which are a different product form; excludes ready-to-drink chocolate and malted milk beverages, which are liquid dairy or plant drinks and route to Category 24 or the plant-milk rows; excludes any mix carrying a Supplement Facts panel, which routes to Category 16. The row is certified in the as-sold dry powder basis because that is the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples, and because the binding instruments are themselves written in that basis; no reconstitution factor is applied to convert the ceiling into an as-consumed beverage value.
cocoa-beverage-mixes.basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight|portion ordinarily consumed
cocoa-beverage-mixes.basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard. This row's guard additionally admits the FSANZ basis phrase (portion ordinarily consumed), which binds the cadmium cell. That phrase denotes the edible portion of the food as listed rather than a prepared serving, so for a powder consumed in its entirety it coincides with the as-sold dry article this row publishes, and no reconstitution or dilution factor is applied. The admission is narrow and row-specific: it is not extended to the other dry rows in this category, none of which has an FSANZ anchor.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a lead maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. This is a real and consequential gap, and it is disclosed rather than filled. EU 2023/915 writes cadmium cells for cocoa powder and for every chocolate cocoa-solids band but no lead cell for any of them; Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Health Canada and Hong Kong Cap 132V likewise set no lead maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or malted drink powder. The read-across candidates were examined and all rejected: the Hong Kong Milk cell (20 ug/kg) is an as-consumed liquid value and applying it to a dry powder that is reconstituted at roughly one part in ten would be a basis conflation in the strict direction; the sugar cells cover a different, refined commodity that supplies little of a mix's lead; the tea and coffee commodity cells are unrelated botanicals. Lead is the analyte of greatest concern in cocoa supply chains, so this control is written with a hard escalation rule rather than a soft one. Lead is a Tier-1 analyte, so a control here means mandatory lot testing with an escalation rule, not an absence of scrutiny; no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
control.reference_method: Lead by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold basis, reported on the certificate. Any result above 100 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient-origin, milling and equipment investigation and blocks certification pending resolution; results feed the Standards Ratchet trigger pool under Governance Policy section 12.

Cd.label: Two credible sovereigns write a cadmium cell that reaches this exact product form. FSANZ Schedule 19 sets 500 ug/kg for chocolate AND COCOA PRODUCTS, which covers a drinking-cocoa powder on its face; EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.2.15.4 sets 600 ug/kg for cocoa powder placed on the market for the final consumer or as an ingredient in sweetened cocoa powder or powdered chocolate, which names this row's sweetened and powdered-chocolate mixes explicitly; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets 2000 ug/kg for cocoa powder ready for consumption. All three are named; the FSANZ cell is the strictest applicable and binds.
Cd.basis_label: dry cocoa or drinking-chocolate powder as sold (edible portion, no reconstitution applied)
Cd.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup across three named sovereign cells, taking the strictest applicable rather than the most convenient. The FSANZ cell binds at 500 ug/kg: its scope phrase reaches cocoa products generally rather than confectionery only, so it applies to a drinking-cocoa or hot-chocolate powder without any extension of scope, and it is stricter than the EU cell that names this form most precisely. Its basis, the portion ordinarily consumed, is the edible portion of the food as listed, which for a powder that is consumed in its entirety is the powder as sold; no reconstitution factor is applied, and if the phrase were instead read as the prepared drink the FSANZ ceiling would be an order of magnitude stricter still, so adopting it on the as-sold powder is the conservative reading in the applicant's favour and is disclosed as such. The stricter cells the audit scan flags are all CHOCOLATE CONFECTIONERY bands and are rejected on scope, not on convenience: EU 2023/915 writes a cocoa-solids band structure for chocolate (milk chocolate under 30 percent dry cocoa solids at 100 ug/kg, chocolate under 50 percent at 300 ug/kg, chocolate at or above 50 percent at 800 ug/kg) and Hong Kong writes the same structure (300 to 900 ug/kg), and both drafted those bands alongside a separate, dedicated cell for the drinking powder. Eating chocolate is a different product form, excluded from this row by its own scope note and routed to the confectionery category. Method v2.0 step 4 requires HMTc to preserve the product-form split the government itself wrote rather than to import a confectionery band into a beverage powder because it produces a lower number. Cadmium in cocoa is origin-driven and well characterised, so this cell is a declared Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12; occurrence data may inform surveillance but may not select the number.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. No sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic cell for this commodity either, so both arsenic cells in this row are controls and the escalation rule carries the obligation. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell is scoped either to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to packaged and public drinking water. None of those is applicable to this dry commodity, and applying a ready-to-drink beverage cell to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation. Inorganic arsenic is a Tier-1 analyte, so it is speciated whenever the total-arsenic screen is elevated.
control.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot exceeds 100 ug/kg in the as-sold dry basis; a confirmed inorganic-arsenic result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a dry cocoa or malted beverage powder: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.

Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 sets nickel at 15000 ug/kg for cocoa powder and fat-reduced cocoa powder, and the register row records the instrument's own parenthetical for that cell, drinking chocolate. This is a DIRECT sovereign maximum level for this row's product form and basis and it binds; the cell applies from 1 July 2025.
Ni.basis_label: product as placed on market, dry cocoa or drinking-chocolate powder
Ni.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. The chocolate nickel bands in the same instrument (milk chocolate under 30 percent dry cocoa solids at 2500 ug/kg, milk chocolate at or above 30 percent and chocolate at 7000 ug/kg) are stricter but are written for eating chocolate, a different product form that this row excludes; adopting one of them because it is lower would be reaching past the instrument's scope, and the EU drafters wrote the cocoa-powder cell at 15000 knowing those bands existed. Cocoa is a genuine nickel accumulator, which is why the EU's own cocoa-powder value is the highest nickel cell in the instrument outside the seaweeds; the number is published as written. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a tin maximum level for a dry cocoa or malted beverage powder. The exclusion is written into the instrument itself: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5 scopes its inorganic-tin maximum levels to canned beverages and canned foods and expressly excepts canned dried and canned powdered products, and the Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong canned-food cells carry the same carve-out. There is therefore no sovereign number for a dry beverage commodity and no supportable read-across, because the canned-liquid cells are written in a ready-to-drink basis. Tin is nonetheless on the mandatory eight-total panel.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. Where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink form of this product, that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin maximum level in the as-consumed basis.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable: the only sovereign aluminium values are packaged-drinking-water quality standards written in a litre-of-water basis (Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1). Applying a water-basis value to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation of roughly three orders of magnitude. Aluminium is a live cell for this row: cocoa is grown on acidic tropical soils where plant-available aluminium is elevated, and alkalised (Dutch-process) cocoa carries a processing-aid route as well. Both are investigated on an elevated result.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: this row's certified article is a DRY powder, and alkalised cocoa is mildly ALKALINE rather than acidic, which is the condition under which Cr(VI) is most stable rather than least; the acidic-beverage reduction argument is therefore not merely unavailable but pointing the other way. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
